comments.author: hayley-patton
comments.story: In defense of complicated programming languages
comments.why: Sussman argues ambiguous math notation makes physics hard; programs clarify
comments.text: > But humans dislike, and much prefer infix with its complicated operator precedences Depends on what you're writing; Gerald Jay Sussman claims that edge cases in mathematical notation (and corner-cutting of sorts in what is written) makes physics quite hard to grasp in "The role of programming" [1]; hence the Structure and Interpretation of Classical Mechanics book, which includes many Scheme programs which explicate everything. [1] [VIDEO]
